lessons.title: હું વાંચતો હતો (hũ vā̃cto hato) — was reading, used to read
lessons.gloss: I was reading — the ongoing or habitual past, -to with hato, and a scene with jyāre … tyāre

segments.text: Say "I don't read", the A2 way. (hũ nathī vā̃cto.) Keep its -તો. Then say "I was at home". (hũ ghare hato.)
હું પુસ્તક વાંચતો હતો. hũ pustak vā̃cto hato. — "I was reading a book."
The stem takes -તો, then comes હતો, and both follow the person:

utterances: who: a man. was reading: વાંચતો હતો (vā̃cto hato).
who: a woman. was reading: વાંચતી હતી (vā̃ctī hatī).
who: a neuter thing. was reading: વાંચતું હતું (vā̃ctũ hatũ).
who: several, or respect. was reading: વાંચતા હતા (vā̃ctā hatā).

segments.text: There is no -એ here, even with an object: મીરા ચા પીતી હતી (Mīrā cā pītī hatī), "Mira was drinking tea". The doer form goes with the plain past, પીધી.
The same form tells what used to happen: પહેલાં અરુણ રોજ ચાલતો હતો (pahelā̃ Aruṇ roj cālto hato), "Arun used to walk every day".

blocks.title: You'll want to know: the scene and the event

segments.text: હું વાંચતો હતો ત્યારે ફોન આવ્યો. hũ vā̃cto hato tyāre phon āvyo. — "I was reading when the phone rang."

વાંચતો હતો is the scene: it was going on. આવ્યો is the event that broke in. ત્યારે (tyāre), "at that time", joins them, and જ્યારે can open the scene: જ્યારે અરુણ ઘરે પહોંચ્યો, ત્યારે મીરા રાંધતી હતી (jyāre Aruṇ ghare pahõcyo, tyāre Mīrā rā̃dhtī hatī), "when Arun got home, Mira was cooking".

segments.instruction: "Mira was cooking when Arun came home" — Mīrā rā̃dhtī hatī tyāre Aruṇ ghare āvyo
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "Mira was cooking when Arun came home" — *Mīrā rā̃dhtī hatī tyāre Aruṇ ghare āvyo*]

segments.prompt: Say that you were reading when the phone rang.
acceptedResponses: hũ vā̃cto (vā̃ctī) hato (hatī) tyāre phon āvyo
હું વાંચતો હતો ત્યારે ફોન આવ્યો.
હું વાંચતી હતી ત્યારે ફોન આવ્યો.
hũ vā̃ctī hatī tyāre phon āvyo

feedback.correct: vā̃cto hato for the scene, āvyo for the event.
feedback.incorrect: The reading went on: vā̃cto hato. The phone came once: phon āvyo. Join them with tyāre.

segments.text: "She was reading"? (તે વાંચતી હતી.) Which part is the scene in હું વાંચતો હતો (hũ vā̃cto hato) ત્યારે ફોન આવ્યો? (વાંચતો હતો.) "Mira was drinking tea": મીરા or મીરાએ? (મીરા.)
Before the new one: ask "what happened?" the A2 way. (શું થયું?, śũ thayũ?) Then say "it was raining". (varsād paḍto hato.)
ગઈકાલે રાતે શું બન્યું? gaīkāle rāte śũ banyũ? — "What happened last night?"

શું થયું? is the everyday question. બનવું (banvũ) is for an event, a thing that takes place, and it suits a story. It takes no object, so its past follows its subject, as ગયો does: બન્યું, બન્યો, બની.
અરુણ દાક્તર બન્યો. Aruṇ dāktar banyo. — "Arun became a doctor."

બનવું (banvũ) sits beside બનાવવું, "to make", which you know: one makes a thing, the other is what a thing does when it comes about. CDIAL lists it under Sanskrit vanati, "desires, gains, makes ready", and marks the Gujarati verb as taken from Hindi bannā (CDIAL 11260).

segments.instruction: "What happened last night?" — gaīkāle rāte śũ banyũ?
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "What happened last night?" — *gaīkāle rāte śũ banyũ?*]

segments.instruction: "This used to happen every day" — āvũ roj bantũ hatũ
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "This used to happen every day" — *āvũ roj bantũ hatũ*]

segments.text: What does બનવું (banvũ) mean? ("To happen; to become".) "Arun became a doctor"? (અરુણ દાક્તર બન્યો.) Which question is the everyday one? (શું થયું?)
